title: An invoiced work order's Bill To is read-only with the invoiced tooltip
custom_preconds:
Preconditions

  • Sign in as an Admin at the test location.
  • Have a new customer for this test, customer A.
  • Have a new customer for this test, customer B, the payer.
  • Have a new work order for this test, work order 1, for customer A, invoiced (not paid), billed to customer B.
custom_steps:
1. Open work order 1.
  2. Expand the Customer card.
  3. Hover over the Bill To field.
custom_expected:
Expected Result

Step 1:

  • Work order 1 opens for customer A, with status Invoiced.

Step 2:

  • The Customer card's "Bill To" field reads customer B's name.

Step 3:

  • The tooltip reads "Invoiced. Reverse the invoice to change who's billed."

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

From: PRD "Bill To", Confluence 1003585538, version 0.5 (6 Nov 2026, pending approval, Chris Ward), read 9 Nov 2026 · Epic SV-12289, story SV-12305 (Story 3, Bill To on the work order and part sale Customer card), story SV-12307 (Story 5, Locked Bill To: invoiced and deposits), story SV-12313 (Story 11, Reverse and invoice again)

  • S5-R1: “When Invoiced, the Bill To field is read-only with M4 as its tooltip.”
  • User Feedback Summary: “M4 | Change the Bill To on an Invoiced document | "Invoiced. Reverse the invoice to change who's billed." | Field tooltip; on click, error toast with "Go To Invoice"”
  • Feature Overview, Core Bill To: “Once invoiced, the Bill To is locked. The only correction is to reverse the invoice, change the Bill To and invoice again.”
  • Key Decisions: “Invoiced means locked; Reverse and invoice again is the only correction, and Reverse works as today. The invoice is removed, AccountingHub keeps the reversal record, QuickBooks deletes its copy and receives the re-issued invoice, which keeps the same number.”
  • Feature Overview, State by action (Action | Open | Invoiced | Internal or No Charge): “Pick or change the Bill To | Allowed. Refused while deposits are held (M1). | Read-only (M4) | No Bill To”
  • S3-N3: “Invoiced or holding deposits: see Story 5.”
